title: Number of Good Ways to Split a String
statement:
Cut the string `s` at one position into a non-empty prefix and a non-empty suffix (the two parts, joined back together, give `s`). Such a cut is good when the prefix and the suffix each contain the same number of different letters.

Return how many of the `s.length - 1` possible cuts are good.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Checking each cut by building both halves and counting their letters costs O(n) per cut, O(n²) overall. Instead, slide the cut from left to right and update counts as one character moves from the right part to the left part. The left part only ever gains letters, so a set of seen letters is enough; the right part loses letters, so it needs a count per letter to know when a letter disappears from it.

## Approach

1. Count every letter of `s` in `rightCount`: before any cut, the whole string is on the right.
2. Start with an empty `leftSeen` set and `good = 0`.
3. For each index `i` from 0 to `s.length - 2`, move `ch = s[i]` to the left: add it to `leftSeen`, decrease its count in `rightCount`, and delete the key when the count reaches 0.
4. Now the cut sits just after `i`; if `leftSeen.size` equals `rightCount.size`, the cut is good, so increase `good`.
5. Return `good`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "aacaba"`, so `rightCount` starts as `{a: 4, c: 1, b: 1}`.

| `i` | `ch` | `leftSeen` | `rightCount` after | sizes | `good` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | a | {a} | {a: 3, c: 1, b: 1} | 1 vs 3 | 0 |
| 1 | a | {a} | {a: 2, c: 1, b: 1} | 1 vs 3 | 0 |
| 2 | c | {a, c} | {a: 2, b: 1} | 2 vs 2 | 1 |
| 3 | a | {a, c} | {a: 1, b: 1} | 2 vs 2 | 2 |
| 4 | b | {a, c, b} | {a: 1} | 3 vs 1 | 2 |

The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to count and one pass to slide the cut.
- Space: O(1): at most 26 keys in the map and the set.

## Pitfalls

- Stop the loop at `s.length - 2`: both parts must be non-empty, so there are only `s.length - 1` cuts.
- Delete a letter from `rightCount` when its count hits 0; otherwise `rightCount.size` overcounts the right part's letters.
- Compare the number of different letters, not the lengths of the two parts.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rightCount` | for each letter still in the right part, how many times it appears there |
| `leftSeen` | the distinct letters in the left part |
| `good` | number of good cuts found so far |
| `i` | index of the last character of the left part |
| `ch` | the character moving from right to left |
